output.subject: Thank you for your kind words about our Elm & 4th branch
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

We are so sorry for the loss of your father. Thank you for taking the time to write to us during what must be a very difficult period.

You told us you had been dreading closing out your dad's accounts, and that our colleague at the Elm & 4th branch walked you through every step. You mentioned they found a CD that none of your family knew about, and that they called you back when one of your forms was kicked back. It means a great deal to hear that someone helped make this process feel more manageable for you.

We have received your message, and we are sharing your thanks so it can be recognized. There is nothing further you need to do. If any questions come up as you finish settling your father's affairs, please don't hesitate to get in touch.

With our sincere condolences and thanks,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: This is a compliment, not a complaint; intake mode was ACKNOWLEDGE ONLY, so the draft thanks the customer rather than promising a specialist review or a 10-business-day response. Confirm this approach.
Staff member's name was redacted (⟦NAME_1⟧); decide whether to name them in the reply.
Confirm the compliment will actually be passed to the staff member and branch, since the draft says it is being shared.
Customer is recently bereaved; check whether any estate or account-closure steps are still pending that should be mentioned.
